decisions.claim: The filed hypothesis is REFUTED. This is not MSVC STL layout or constructor-prototype propagation. It is a generic type-lattice escalation: a small-string-optimized object writes the unsatisfiable equation T = ptr(T) into ActionInferTypes (one MULTIEQUAL input is PTRSUB(spacebase,-0xN), typed pointer-to-the-mapped-local; the other is a LOAD from that same address, typed as the local), so the propagation adopts a type exactly one pointer level deeper per pass until the seven-pass settle ceiling.
decisions.evidence: The ActionInferTypes ceiling was made settable and swept 1..12 on the witness: max pointer depth in the emitted C is 2,2,3,4,5,5,5,5 -- one level per pass. Tracing every candidate of depth>=3 that propagate_type_edge adopted: 1368 INDIRECT, 958 MULTIEQUAL, 84 PTRSUB, 44 COPY, 42 PTRADD, 4 STORE, 4 INT_EQUAL; every PTRSUB is in0->out-1 off register:0x20 (RSP). Reproduced with no C++ at all on a 0x131-byte hand-built x86-64 ELF bytechunk (tests/stages/kuna-ptrdepthcap.xml).

decisions.claim: The captain's `scope: large` triage followed from the (wrong) hypothesis. The fix is one focused change, not a C++ type-recovery project, so the proposal fork was NOT taken.
decisions.evidence: Upstream already has the rule (TypeFactory::getTypePointerNoDepth, type.cc:1509); Ghidra just never calls it on the spacebase-PTRSUB arm. Shipped as one new module (p5_types/kuna_ptrdepth.rs), one gated call site in propagate_type_edge, one settable row. No new pass, no new pass type, no ported-core anchor files touched.

decisions.claim: The acceptance probe as filed was gameable and was tightened before being relied on -- never relaxed.
decisions.evidence: a-4ac515df8701 asserted only stdout_absent of the two ***** spellings with NO exit_code clause, so a crash, a timeout or an empty decompile would have passed it. Added: exit_code eq 0; stdout_absent "\\*\\*\\*" (no three-deep pointer anywhere); stdout_matches on all four string literals the tester had to hand-track. 8/8 clauses PASS.

decisions.claim: verify --promote correctly refuses this acceptance and no in-repo fixture was fabricated to get around it.
decisions.evidence: The target is binary_source: dataset (bin/trappy attack.exe) and CI has no dataset -- the same refusal PR #377 got. The in-repo regression cover is the two-pass tests/stages/kuna-ptrdepthcap.xml plus 8 unit tests.

decisions.claim: The mechanism does not delete, move or re-anchor a statement, and does not lose a call.
decisions.evidence: 90 binaries / 22,307 functions A/B'd whole-binary. 103 change; the call-name multiset per function is IDENTICAL on both arms for all 103 (0 lost, 0 gained). 98 are type-only by statement skeleton; the 5 with statement-level differences were read line by line and every residual is an addressing spelling. One named degradation: an 8-byte zero store re-rendering as eight one-byte stores where the object really is an array of 8-byte pointers -- 12 lines, 2 functions.

decisions.claim: The cap does not remove every deep pointer, and that is stated rather than hidden.
decisions.evidence: Across the sweep, three-or-more-star occurrences fall 1,617 -> 28 and the functions carrying one 80 -> 17. The residual 17 are not reached by propagate_type_edge (declared/locked types and pointer-relative types), so this option cannot and does not touch them.

speed_note: Primary figure is the INERT target: crakersme.exe, 1,027 functions, output byte-identical on both arms -- decompile-all -0.12% min / +0.05% median against an on-vs-on control of -0.10% / -0.04%, so the per-edge hook is free. Where the option fires it is not free: the witness binary (144 functions, 1 changes) is +5.3% whole-binary and the witness function alone +8.5% on the minimum, i.e. ~40 ms confined to the one function whose lattice now settles instead of freezing at the ceiling. All randomized-interleaved with an on-vs-on control arm; a FIXED A/B/A order on this box reported -29% between two identical arms, so the ordering had to be randomized before any number meant anything.
